subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a content-bearing cross-session self-activity record, and exactly which Slack workspace, account, channel or thread, requester, retention, and deletion rules should govern DM access to it?
rationale: The source behavior is clear, but the requested capability crosses an intentional session-content boundary and cannot safely reuse transcript visibility or the metadata-only audit contract without maintainer policy.

options.title: Approve scoped records
options.body: Add a bounded shared-state SQLite record and agent-facing query limited to the same agent’s successful outbound messages and explicitly authorized Slack destinations.

options.title: Keep current isolation
options.body: Retain destination-only transcripts and require explicit memory or session workflows for cross-context continuity.

options.title: Broaden transcript visibility
options.body: Let DM sessions inspect sibling channel histories, accepting substantially wider content disclosure than this request requires.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped records
recommendation.body: Add a bounded shared-state SQLite record and agent-facing query limited to the same agent’s successful outbound messages and explicitly authorized Slack destinations.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the core outbound-mirroring behavior, has the strongest recent Slack/outbound history, and already framed the unresolved product/privacy boundary on this issue.
